data_notes: league.json shows Total Managers = 0 and empty template/differentials arrays — mini-league EO is unusable for GW1. All EO figures below are web-sourced overall-FPL ownership plus modelled captain share.

xpts.json carries no selected_by_percent field, so template proxy = published pre-deadline ownership (FFScout ownership watch 12 Aug, FFFix template team, OneFPL final GW1 template) cross-checked against xpts rank.
EO estimate = own% + captain%. Captain share is modelled from published captain polls (Haaland dominant, Bruno clear second), not an official feed — treat as +/- 10pp.
GW1 has no form/price history, so ownership dispersion is at its season-low: the template is at its most concentrated and template-fade risk is at its season-high.

captain_shield.why: THE shield pick of GW1 and the single biggest EO object on the board. ~70% owned and mass-captained (~55% armband share) gives EO ~125%. A Haaland brace is roughly a 24-30pt EO swing against anyone without him. Historically a fast starter. The backtest lesson (fading template captains cost points) applies here in its purest form — but we DO NOT OWN HIM, so this is a rank_risk we cannot shield with the armband, only with a transfer.

The shield we actually hold, and the current armband. Highest xPts in the model (9.13) and the clear #2 captain in public polls (~18% share), so if he hauls the damage of not captaining him is real. High floor: penalties, set pieces, nailed 90 minutes, FDR 2. Projection gap to Haaland is inside noise (published 6.8 vs 6.6). sim-lab / gaffer: do NOT move the armband off Bruno onto a sub-20% EO asset — that is the exact double-fade (no Haaland AND no template-adjacent captain) that produced the worst backtest rounds.

Current vice. Official-FPL must-have defender at ~25% own with xPts 8.34 and FDR 2. High-floor clean-sheet plus aerial-goal threat. Fine as VC insurance, but not a captain per APEX cum_pts rule (defender, no season cum_pts yet).

differentials.why: Named in multiple published GW1 low-owned lists. Model xPts 5.92 is top-15 overall and the best of any sub-10% forward. Nailed penalties and Brentford's lone striker — his ceiling is a brace plus bonus. Best differential we already own; the free roll of the squad.

Sub-5% midfielder at 6.0m with xPts 5.28 and FDR 2. Sunderland set-piece and creative hub. Genuine rank-gain asset because virtually nobody in the top 10k carries him — but a low-floor pick, start him, never captain him.
Attacking wing-back with two pre-season assists at 5.5m. Attacking-return ceiling of a midfielder from a defender slot at ~10% ownership. Rotation is the risk, not the ceiling.

TARGET (not owned). Repeatedly flagged as 'template points at differential ownership' — 6.5m with xPts 5.55 and a City attacking-mid role. ~90% of managers do not own him. Best non-Haaland transfer target if the gaffer wants rank upside rather than shielding.
TARGET (not owned). xPts 7.03 is 6th overall in the model, FDR 2, and he sits nowhere near the published template. Highest ceiling-per-ownership asset on the board this week.
TARGET (not owned). 5.0m defender with xPts 6.66 and FDR 2 — clean sheet plus attacking-return profile at cheap-enabler price. Enables a Haaland upgrade if funds are the blocker.

rank_risks.risk: NO HAALAND — the defining rank risk of GW1
rank_risks.detail: Haaland is ~70% owned with ~55% captain share (EO ~125%). The squad has zero exposure. If he returns a brace we lose roughly 24-30 points to the field in a single gameweek, and in GW1 that is a six-figure overall-rank move because everyone starts level. This is precisely the failure mode the backtest identified: fading the template captain. Model xPts has him only 4th (8.13) which UNDERSTATES him — a City opener at FDR 3 is a bad reason to be the only manager without the best striker in the world.
rank_risks.mitigation: Squad value cannot absorb 15.5m without a double-downgrade. If the gaffer will not fund Haaland this week, ACCEPT the risk explicitly and hedge by keeping the armband on the highest-EO owned asset (B.Fernandes) rather than compounding with a maverick captain. Re-evaluate as a GW2/GW3 priority transfer.

rank_risks.detail: Without Haaland, moving the armband off B.Fernandes onto any sub-20% EO asset (Gabriel, Semenyo, Thiago, Raya-type) stacks two independent template fades in one week. Backtest evidence says this is the highest-variance, lowest-EV configuration available.
rank_risks.mitigation: Lock B.Fernandes (C). Flagged to sim-lab and the-gaffer as do-not-override.

rank_risks.detail: Second-largest raw ownership gap after Haaland. A 43%-owned midfielder returning is a ~5-6pt EO leak. Model rates him modestly (xPts 4.92), so this is a tolerable fade — note it, do not chase it.

rank_risks.risk: Missing Guéhi / O'Reilly / Raya cluster (24-31% EO each)
rank_risks.detail: Three separate mid-20s-to-30s ownership blocks we do not hold. Individually survivable; collectively it means our defence and goalkeeper are off-template. Offset is that Gabriel + Calafiori + Lammens give us 3 template-adjacent defensive assets, so net exposure is acceptable.

rank_risks.risk: Bench is deep off-template (Rushworth, Awoniyi, van Ewijk all COV, FDR 5)
rank_risks.detail: Three Coventry assets on the bench with sub-1% ownership and FDR 5. No EO downside (nobody owns them) but zero autosub value if a starter is benched or blanks. Consistency Rule (A) rotation gate applies — do not promote any of them.

rank_risks.risk: Three MUN starters (Lammens, B.Fernandes, Mbeumo) plus captain on MUN
rank_risks.detail: Correlated exposure. A heavy United defeat torches the goalkeeper clean sheet, two midfielders AND the doubled captain simultaneously. This is the concentrated downside that pairs with the no-Haaland upside gap — the week is genuinely high-variance in both directions.

summary.captain_shield_verdict: DO NOT FADE — highest owned EO asset, highest model xPts, clear #2 public armband
summary.unshieldable_risk: Haaland (EO ~125%) not owned — accept and note, or fund a transfer
